Hanafuda

A Japanese 48-card deck divided into 12 suits, one for each month of the year. Each suit depicts a seasonal flower or plant. Multiple completely different games are played with this deck.

The 48-Card Deck

12 suits of 4 cards each. Within each suit, cards are ranked by type: Bright, Animal, Ribbon, Plain.

Month Suit (Flower) Bright Animal Ribbon Plains
January Pine Crane + Sun — Red Poetry 2
February Plum Blossom — Bush Warbler Red Poetry 2
March Cherry Blossom Cherry Curtain — Red Poetry 2
April Wisteria — Cuckoo Red 2
May Iris — Bridge Red 2
June Peony — Butterflies Blue 2
July Bush Clover — Boar Red 2
August Pampas Grass Full Moon Geese — 2
September Chrysanthemum — Sake Cup Blue 2
October Maple — Deer Blue 2
November Willow Rain Man Swallow Lightning 1
December Paulownia Phoenix — — 3

Totals: 5 Brights, 9 Animals, 10 Ribbons, 24 Plains = 48 cards.

Ribbon types:

  • Red Poetry (Akatan): Pine, Plum, Cherry — marked with calligraphy
  • Plain Red: Wisteria, Iris, Bush Clover
  • Blue (Aotan): Peony, Chrysanthemum, Maple
  • Lightning (special): Willow (November)

Games

  • Go-Stop — Korean hanafuda (Hwatu deck). Most popular card game in South Korea. Go/Stop decision: press on for bigger rewards or bank winnings. 2–3 players.
  • Hana-Awase — The base matching game. Collect cards by suit, highest point value wins.
  • Koi-Koi — Two-player matching game. Complete a yaku (scoring pattern), then choose: stop and score, or call “koi-koi” to continue for higher stakes.
  • Oicho-Kabu — Betting game using month values (mod 10). Closest to 9 wins. Origin of the word “Yakuza.”
